extracted: Death was the only outcome: no breathing, blood level or other measure of tolerance was taken at any point. The authors propose a model of overdose deaths in which tolerance fails where the drug is given in an environment not previously associated with it, describe the design as a methodologically rigorous demonstration of the contribution of contextual stimuli to tolerance, read the DT-ST difference as showing that identical drug histories need not produce equal tolerance to heroin's lethal effect, and conclude that rats given the high dose among cues previously associated with lower doses were more likely to survive than rats given it among cues not associated with the drug.
